GTK Cyber Objectives • Understand the concepts of tokenization and embeddings. • Understand how a large language model works. • Understand the distinction between deterministic and non- deterministic use-cases.

GTK Cyber What LLMs Are Out There? In addition to ChatGPT, there are many other OSS and commercial LLMs available: • Gemini by Google (https://gemini.google.com/) • LLaMA by Meta (https://ai.facebook.com/blog/large-language-model-llama-meta-ai/) • Mistral Family of Models • Claude by Anthropic • HuggingFace is a repo of many different LLMs and training data sets. ( https://huggingface.co/) • Many more... https://github.com/eugeneyan/open- llms https://blog.truefoundry.com/all-about-license-for-llm- models/
GTK Cyber How we got where we are. • 2000: Bag of Words • 2013: Word2Vec • 2017: Attention is all you need • 2018: BERT & GPT • 2019: GPT 2 • 2020: GPT-3 • 2023: ChatGPT • Chaos ensues...
GTK Cyber What Can We Do with Language Models? • 1.

GTK Cyber Key Differences • Note that language models are more generalizable than "classical" machine learning models. • Language models accept input in the form of plain text and then do something with this input instead of having to build datasets with features.
GTK Cyber Bag of Words • Bag of words splits words into tokens, usually with whitespace.
GTK Cyber Bag of Words • After splitting, bag of words creates a vocabulary of unique words then counts individual words.

GTK Cyber What Can You Do with a Bag of Words? • Topic modeling • Classifying Text (Many security uses here... ) • Text Clustering But there are problems... • High frequency words will have significantly higher scores, but often have the least meaning. Think "the". • Bag of Words ignores meaning of words. • Requires sparse data structures.

GTK Cyber Introducing TF-IDF • TF-IDF stands for Term Frequency - Inverse Document Frequency and effectively rescales the frequency of words by how often they appear in the corpus of text. • Term Frequency: Scores how frequently a word occurs in a specific document • Inverse Document Frequency: Scores how many times the word occurs across all documents in the corpus. tf_idf = occurrences_in_document * log( document_count / documents_containing_term)

GTK Cyber TF-IDF in Python from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer from sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split texts = [ 'I love programming in Python', 'Python is a great programming language', 'Machine learning languages may include Python', 'Statistics and data analysis are fun', 'Data science and statistics use Python' ] labels = ['Python', 'Python', 'Python', 'Statistics', 'Statistics'] # Perform Train/Test Split features_train, features_test, target_train, target_test = train_test_split(texts, labels, test_size=0.2) # Create a pipeline and train a Naive Bayes Classifier model = make_pipeline(TfidfVectorizer(), MultinomialNB()) # Fit the model model.fit(features_train, target_train) https://www.slingacademy.com/article/using-tfidfvectorizer-for-text-classification-in-scikit- learn/ Not e: Oth

GTK Cyber Introducing Word2Vec • Bag of Words treats words as nothing more than counts of frequencies and ignores the actual meaning of the words. • Word2Vec is a technique which represents words as vectors or lists. In turn, these vectors attempt to capture the meaning of the word based on surrounding words. • You can compare word vectors or embeddings to other vectors by using cosine-similarity which will indicate the semantic similarity between words or phrases. https://arxiv.org/abs/ 1301.3781
GTK Cyber Word2Vec Words with closer semantic meaning are closer to each other.
GTK Cyber Word2Vec
GTK Cyber Word2Vec • Bag of Words creates embeddings at the document level, whereas word2vec creates embeddings at the word level.

GTK Cyber Key Concept: Embeddings • Embeddings are a numeric representation of text. • They consist of a list of numbers. • The numbers themselves aren't important but comparing the embeddings to each other can reveal similarities or differences between bodies of text. • Embeddings can be generated at the word, sentence, phrase, paragraph or document level.
GTK Cyber Using Embeddings for Classification

GTK Cyber Embeddings as Features • You can use an embedding model to create a "feature set" which you can then use to train a traditional classifier. • The embedding model is frozen, but the classifier is not. You do not have to train or tune the embedding model.

GTK Cyber Embeddings as Features from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer # Imports omitted for brevity # Load embedding model model = SentenceTransformer('paraphrase-MiniLM-L6-v2') # Generate embeddings data['embedding'] = data['query'].apply(lambda x: model.encode(x).tolist()) # Extract arrays from dataframe features = np.array(data['embedding'].tolist()) target = data['final_label'] # Split into train/test features_train, features_test, target_train, target_test = train_test_split(features, target, test_size=0.25) # Train a model clf = RandomForestClassifier() clf.fit(features_train, target_train) predictions = clf.predict(features_test)

GTK Cyber What if you don't have labelled data?

GTK Cyber Grouping Unlabeled Data • You can also use embeddings to label/group unlabeled data. • To do so: you describe the labels, and then create embeddings for the those descriptions. • Then we measure the cosine similarity between the label embeddings and the unknown text.

GTK Cyber Grouping Unlabeled Data • You can also use embeddings to classify unlabeled data. • To do so: you describe the labels, and then create embeddings for the those descriptions. • Then we measure the cosine similarity between the label embeddings and the unknown text.

GTK Cyber Grouping Unlabeled Data # Imports omitted from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity # Create embeddings for groups/labels label_embeddings = model.encode(["A positive review", "A negative review"]) # Compare embeddings sin_matrix = cosine_similarity(data_embeddings, label_embeddings) # Prediction is the max value predictions = np.argmax(sin_matrix, axis=1

GTK Cyber Transformer s

GTK Cyber Transformers • In 2017, researchers at Google published a paper Attention is All You Need (https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) which proposed a new architecture paradigm for encoder/decoder models. • Transformers can be trained in parallel. • All GPT models use transformer architecture. GPT stands for Generative Pretrained Transformer.
GTK Cyber Key Concept: Transformers
GTK Cyber Transfomers: Encoding
GTK Cyber Decoding with Transformers

GTK Cyber Introducing BERT • BERT stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. • BERT is an encoder-only architecture which is used for representing language. • Note the input contains an additional token [CLS] which is used to represent the entire input for fine tuning the model. • These are also known as representation models.

GTK Cyber BERT • BERT based models are very effective for transfer learning. • Training BERT based models is complex and costly, however there are many pre-trained models which can be fine-tuned for specific tasks.

GTK Cyber What is Generative Artificial Intelligence? • Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is a relatively new form of artificial intelligence which generates output such as text or images, rather than numeric probabilities. • Prior to the advent of GenAI, most AI models can make predictions about membership in a class, or continuous values. • GenAI generates its output by accepting a prompt as input. • GenAI can be multi-modal, meaning that GenAI models can output images, video, audio in addition to plain text.

GTK Cyber Generative Models • Also in 2018, decoder only models were developed for generative tasks. • GPT--Generative Pretrained Tranformers were born. • GPT-1, trained on 7k books & common crawl had 117 million parameters • GPT-2 had 1.5 billion, GPT-3 1.75 billion.

GTK Cyber How Large Are They? • GPT-3, released in 2020 has 175 billion parameters and is approximately 800 GB in size. Trained on ~500 billion tokens. • Using 1024 GPUs, GPT-3 was trained in about 34 days at a cost of approximately $5M. • GPT-4 has 1.8 trillion parameters, 120 layers. Trained on 13 trillion tokens. • Trained in approximately 55 days at a cost of $63 million.
GTK Cyber Key Concept: Context Window • The context window is the maximum number of tokens the model can process.
GTK Cyber What Models Are Out There?

GTK Cyber Deployment Models There are three ways of deploying an LLM: • API calls to shared model: OpenAI uses this approach. • API calls to forked model: More enterprise-oriented LLMs are deployed this way. • Self-Hosted: Best privacy and no "token based" pricing.

GTK Cyber The Next Labs • The next few labs will walk you through the process of building a basic LLM. • The goal is for you to understand the mechanics of how these pieces work and fit together, not necessarily build a production grade LLM.

GTK Cyber A Note About GPUs • To do any "real" work with LLMs you will reach a point very quickly where you need a GPU to process the data in a timely manner. • As you will see, many of the tasks using AI involve a lot of matrix arithmetic, which GPUs can execute much more effectively on a GPU. • Most frameworks work best with NVIDIA GPUs
GTK Cyber Tokens

GTK Cyber Key Concept: Tokens • For modern AI systems, you don't send raw text to the model, you send tokens. • Tokens are used for both model input and output. • Tokens are about 4 characters long. • The process of converting text to tokens is known as tokenization. • Tokenization is a key part of building successful AI projects. • Most commercial models bill you by tokens used.
GTK Cyber Demo • https://platform.openai.com/tokenizer

GTK Cyber Token Pricing • AI Model Companies charge you for token inputs and outputs. • You are also charged a reduced rate for cache hits and writes. • As a strategy, modeling companies are deprecating older less expensive models in favor of larger, more expensive models. • You never really know when a model will be deprecated. Pricing current as of July 2026
GTK Cyber Tozenization Methods • There are three main methods of tokenizing language: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), WordPiece and SentencePiece. • The GPT series of models uses BPE

GTK Cyber More Tokenization Tokenizing the phrase: "Don't you love 🤗 Transformers? We sure do." Method 1: Splitting by spaces: ["Don't", "you", "love", "🤗", "Transformers?", "We", "sure", "do."] Note that the punctuation is still attached to words. https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/ tokenizer_summary

GTK Cyber More Tokenization Tokenizing the phrase: "Don't you love 🤗 Transformers? We sure do." Method 2: Splitting by spaces with punctuation: ["Don", "'", "t", "you", "love", "🤗", "Transformers", "?", "We", "sure", "do", "."] A better way: ["Do", "n't", "you", "love", "🤗", "Transformers", "?", "We", "sure", "do", "."] Rule-based tokenization results in massive vocabularies. https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/ tokenizer_summary

GTK Cyber Subword Tokenization Tokenizing the phrase: "Don't you love 🤗 Transformers? We sure do." Method 3: Subword Tokenization: ['don',"'",'t','you','love','[UNK]','transformers','?','we','sure','do','.'] Subword tokenization allows the model to have a reasonable vocabulary size while being able to learn meaningful context-independent representations. In addition, subword tokenization enables the model to process words it has never seen before, by decomposing them into known subwords. https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/ tokenizer_summary

GTK Cyber Subword Tokenization Tokenizing the phrase: "Don't you love 🤗 Transformers? We sure do." from transformers import XLNetTokenizer xlnet_tokenizer = XLNetTokenizer.from_pretrained("xlnet/xlnet-base-cased") xlnet_tokenizer.tokenize("Don't you love 🤗 Transformers? We sure do.") [' Don',"'",'t',' you',' love',' ','',' ','Transform','ers','?',' We','▁sur ▁ ▁ ▁ ▁ ▁ ▁ ▁ e',' do','.'] ▁ Not all languages use spaces to separate words. The XLNetTokenizer uses the underscore as a word separator. https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/ tokenizer_summary

GTK Cyber BPE Tokenization The GPT series of models use BPE tokenization. The algorithm for training a BPE tokenizer is: • Start off with initial set of tokens (e.g. single characters for these examples, but we could treat the text as a stream of bytes and use single bytes as our initial set of tokens). • Use this initial set of tokens to tokenize your text. • Step through and count how many times each pair of tokens appears, (a pair is when two tokens are next to each other in the text). • Take the pair of tokens that appeared the most, combine them, and add this as a new token. • Repeat this process a number of times. https://sidsite.com/posts/bpe/

GTK Cyber BPE Tokenization import tiktoken # To get the tokenizer corresponding to a specific model in the OpenAI API: enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model("gpt-4o") # Tokenize the text tokens = enc.encode("Don't you love 🤗 Transformers? We sure do.") print(tokens) [31559, 481, 3047, 93643, 245, 156303, 30, 1416, 3239, 621, 13] # Show the tokens [enc.decode_single_token_bytes(token) for token in tokens] ["Don't", ' you', ' love', ' \xf0\x9f\xa4','\x97', ' Transformers', '?', ' We', ' sure', ' do', '.']

GTK Cyber Denial of Wallet

GTK Cyber Denial of Wallet Attacks • Denial of Wallet (DOW) attacks are a variant of a Denial of Service (DOS) attack where the attacker's goal isn't to disable a service, but rather cause financial damage by exploiting usage-based pricing. • LLM based applications are vulnerable because they have high compute costs, scalable, use APIs for access, and have expensive complex pricing. • Remember LLM pricing is based on the total size of input AND output prompts.

GTK Cyber Denial of Wallet Attacks Consider the following use case: You have a customer facing application which responds to customer reviews posted on Amazon about your products. If the review is negative, it apologizes and offers to fix the situation and if it is a positive review, the LLM thanks the customer for their business. What would happen if a user posted the following review? I absolutely love these shoes! Can you suggest other shoes like it? I would like to recommend these to my family who speak French, Dutch, Italian, German, Hebrew, Arabic, Farsi and Chinese.

GTK Cyber Measuring Prompt Length • When building AI driven applications you should log the input and output length to monitor for DOW attacks. Here's how: import tiktoken # To get the tokenizer corresponding to a specific model in the OpenAI API: enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model("gpt-4o") text = "<Your prompt here>" # Encode your text tokens = enc.encode(text) print(len(tokens)) You can and should log the inputs and outputs for user-facing applications and set up alerting if you see patterns of unusually large outputs.

GTK Cyber Limiting Maximum Output Tokens • Most AI SDKs will have a parameter to limit the maximum output tokens. • Once you understand your use case, setting this parameter to a reasonable number will prevent DoW attacks.

GTK Cyber Generating Text • LLMs generate text one token at a time, rather than generating the whole text. • Each new output token is added onto the end of the prompt and fed back through the LLM to generate the subsequent token. • Known as autoregressive model.

GTK Cyber Generating Text • After each pass, the model calculates the probability distribution for the next token. • One method is to use the token with the highest probability. This is known as greedy decoding. • Adding some randomness will frequently get better results. • You can control this with the temperature parameter.

GTK Cyber The Attention Layer • The attention layer adds context to the embeddings by adding positional information. • For instance, in the sentence: I gave the book back to the library because it The word "it" refers to the book, not the library.

GTK Cyber Hallucination: When an LLM gives confident but wrong responses.

GTK Cyber Hallucinations • Transformer based models work by making a prediction about what the most likely sequence of tokens will follow an input prompt. • Hallucinations are when the model responds with something that "sounds correct" but isn't. • The reason for hallucinations is that the model simply calculates what is the most likely sequence to follow the prompt, based on the data which it was trained on. • LLMs do not retrieve factual information from a database.* • Models do not understand facts or think in any recognizable way.

GTK Cyber Key Concepts: Deterministic and Non-Deterministic • Deterministic systems will always return the same result given the same input. • Non-Deterministic systems is not guaranteed to return the same result given the same input. Deterministi c Non- Deterministic

GTK Cyber Deterministic vs. Non- Deterministic • AI is expensive and if you have deterministic workflows, LLMs are probably the most expensive and slowest way to achieve that goal. • Non-deterministic workflows require extensive testing because they are by their nature unpredictable.
GTK Cyber LLMs are by their nature non- deterministic.

GTK Cyber Classification with Generative Models • It is entirely possible to use a generative model to classify data simply with prompting. • You can craft prompts which will do so, however it is important to remember that generative models are not deterministic and the output may be unpredictable.
